The Prophet used a sa' to five mudds of water for bathing and one mudd for ablution, and companions saw him wipe over his khuffs and once his turban.
The Prophet prayed without new ablution after eating cooked mutton, and after saweeq only rinsed his mouth, as he did after milk, saying it has fat.
One who grows drowsy while praying should sleep until he knows what he is saying, lest he pray against himself instead of asking forgiveness.
The Prophet made ablution for every prayer while companions kept one until hadath, and after eating saweeq he only rinsed his mouth before praying.
Hearing two people tortured in their graves, one for not guarding against urine and one for calumnies, the Prophet set half a palm leaf on each, hoping to ease it.
Anas brought water whenever the Prophet went to relieve himself, and he cleaned his private parts with it.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said one buried there was punished for not guarding against urine and one for calumnies, and fixed a palm leaf piece on each.
The Prophet had water poured on a Bedouin's urine in the mosque, telling people to make things easy, poured water over a baby's urine, and urinated standing at a dump.
Menstrual blood on clothes is rubbed and washed before praying in them, and bleeding from a vein is not menses, so a woman prays, leaving prayer only during real menses.
Aisha washed semen from the Prophet's clothes, and he went to prayer with the wet spots still visible.
People of Ukl or Uraina, healed by camels' milk and urine, killed the herdsman and drove off the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, water withheld.
Before the mosque was built, the Prophet prayed in sheepfolds.
Asked about ghee into which a mouse had fallen, the Prophet said to remove the mouse and the ghee around it and use the rest.
A wound received in Allah's cause will appear on Resurrection Day bleeding but smelling of musk, and the Muslims, the last to come, will be foremost on that Day.
One should not urinate in still water and then bathe in it.
At the Ka'bah one of Abu Jahl's group put camel entrails on the prostrating Prophet until Fatima removed them; he invoked against Quraysh, naming men later seen dead at Badr.
The Prophet once spat into his clothes.
Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden.
Ali brought water in his shield and Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face, then the ash of a burnt straw mat filled his wound.
The Prophet used the siwak, with a retching sound, including on rising at night, and dreamt he was told to give it to the older of two men.
Before sleep one makes ablution, lies on the right side and supplicates, entrusting oneself to Allah and affirming His Book and Prophet; dying that night, one dies with faith.
In the bath after janaba the Prophet washed his hands, made ablution and poured water over himself; he shared one pot with a wife, and a sa' sufficed.
The Prophet poured water thrice on his head, rubbed scent into it, washed his private parts, cleaned his hand with earth, washed his feet last and declined a towel.
The Prophet and a wife bathed from one pot in turn; he washed his hands first, and Maimuna, who screened him, described each step and how he declined a towel.
Answering Ibn Umar's view, Aisha said she scented the Prophet, he went round his wives, and in the morning he assumed ihram with the scent's fragrance still on him.
Anas said the Prophet visited all his wives, eleven or by another report nine, in one round, day and night, and companions said he had the strength of thirty.
Ali had a man ask the Prophet about frequent urethral discharge, and was told to wash the organ and make ablution.
Aisha scented the Prophet, who went round his wives and was muhrim by morning, and she recalled the glint of scent in his hair parting while he was in ihram.
The Prophet's janaba bath began with ablution and ended with the feet; once he recalled janaba at the iqama and went to bathe, and women pour thrice on the head.
The Children of Israel bathed naked together and claimed Moses, who bathed alone, had a defect, until a stone ran off with his clothes and they saw him unblemished.
While Job bathed naked, golden locusts fell on him and he gathered them, telling his Lord he could never do without His blessings.
Fatima and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed, and he told Um Sulaim a woman must bathe after a wet dream if she sees discharge.
Abu Huraira, junub, slipped away from the Prophet to bathe, and the Prophet told him a believer never becomes impure.
Anas said the Prophet visited all his wives in one night, when he had nine wives.
Junub, Abu Huraira slipped away from the Prophet's side to bathe and found him still sitting on return, and was told that a believer never becomes impure.
A junub person may sleep after washing his private parts and making ablution, as the Prophet did and told Umar.
Intercourse makes the bath compulsory; Uthman and others reported washing and ablution when there is no emission, but the bath is called safer and the final ruling.
Menses, ordained for Adam's daughters, bar only tawaf in Hajj, and while menstruating the Prophet's wives combed his hair, let him recite leaning on their lap, and shared his sheet.
The Prophet had a wife in her menses wear a waist-sheet before fondling her; Aisha shared his bath pot and washed his head during his I'tikaf while menstruating.
At Eid the Prophet told women to give alms, as he saw most of Hell's dwellers were women, and tied their deficiency in intelligence and religion to testimony and menses.
